frontMatter.welcome:
Welcome to Rakheja Enterprises LLP! We are delighted to have you join our journey in the garment industry, where innovation, quality, and sustainability are our guiding principles. Every employee is integral to our success, and we’re excited for the unique skills and dedication you bring. As you begin this journey with us, please take time to familiarize yourself with this handbook, which outlines expectations, policies, and available resources, helping ensure a fulfilling and productive experience
At Rakheja Enterprises LLP, our purpose is to lead in sustainable garment manufacturing, producing quality products responsibly while aligning with global standards. By combining tradition with innovation, we aim to deliver apparel solutions for global markets, meeting modern industry demands with sustainable practices that preserve resources for future generations. This commitment underpins everything we do and reflects our dedication to building a resilient, eco-friendly future for our industry and communities.
Our commitment to excellence drives continuous improvement in three focus areas:
- Enhancing Capabilities: We prioritize skill-building and advanced technologies to expand our garment solutions, offering diverse, eco-friendly products that add value to clients and strengthen industry relationships.
- Innovative Production: By developing custom treatments and expanding our lineup with fire-retardant and water-repellent fabrics, we meet unique client needs, combining function with environmental consciousness.
- Sustainable Value Creation: Sustainability is central to our business. We invest in research and practices that meet industry standards and contribute to a greener planet, creating long-term value for employees, stakeholders, and society.
frontMatter.about: Founded in 1987, Rakheja Enterprises LLP has grown into a respected garment manufacturer. Our specialization in children’s and ladies' woven and knitted garments reflects over three decades of commitment to quality and innovation. We continually invest in eco-friendly practices to meet modern demands for quality and sustainability. Our products embody our legacy and mission: to lead in quality garment production while ensuring environmental responsibility for a more sustainable future.

Understanding this handbook is key to your success and the smooth progression of your journey with us.

- Safe Workplace: We maintain high safety standards, conducting regular inspections to prevent workplace hazards.
- Freedom of Association: Employees can join unions or associations without discrimination or retaliation.

## Probation Period:
- New employees are placed on a 3-month probation period during which their performance is monitored and evaluated regularly. Feedback is provided to ensure the employee’s success and improvement if needed.
- Post-Probation Confirmation: If the employee successfully meets performance expectations, they will receive a confirmation letter from HR, officially acknowledging them as a permanent employee and recognizing their contributions to the team.
## Internal Career Growth and Mobility
## Opportunities for Advancement:
- Rakheja Enterprises LLP values internal career growth, giving priority to internal candidates when filling roles. Openings are announced via email and intranet to encourage internal advancement.
- Support for Internal Transfers: Employees applying for new roles internally go through the same interview process to ensure fairness.
## Policy on Original Documents
## Document Security:

## Record Keeping and Compliance
## Data Security:

## Compensation and Annual Revision Policy
- The compensation and benefits structure at Rakheja Enterprises LLP is pivotal to attracting and retaining top talent, which is essential for the company’s ongoing growth and success. As an established garment export house, we understand the importance of competitive compensation in maintaining our position in the global market. Effective talent management ensures that Rakheja Enterprises LLP remains competitive and continues to meet the demands of both the USA and European markets, where we primarily operate.
- Our company is committed to offering competitive wages that align with or exceed legal requirements, including gender pay equality, ensuring fair and equitable compensation for all employees.
## Annual Compensation Review
We will review employee compensation annually, considering factors like financial health, business performance, market trends, and competitor pay scales. The review will include:
- Business conditions
- Sales forecasts
- Competitor compensation trends
- Individual performance and experience
- Qualifications and job-related skills
The goal is to strike a balance between offering attractive pay and maintaining operational efficiency and cost competitiveness. Pay is determined based on several criteria:
- Importance and criticality of the role
- Responsibilities and key deliverables
- Relevant experience
- Performance and competencies
- Qualifications and educational background
- Market availability of talent
- Compensation trends in the industry
- Internal equity
- Work location

chapters.title: Paternity Leave:
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Permanent male employees are entitled to two days of paternity leave, effective from the date of childbirth. This leave is applicable for a maximum of two children only.
## Additional Weekly Off:
- Eligibility: Deputy Managers and above will receive two additional weekly offs per month, as per government regulations.
## Leave Without Pay (LWP):
- Eligibility: LWP can be availed when other leave types are unavailable or exhausted. A maximum of 30 days of LWP can be taken with prior approval from the Department Head.
## Shift Change:
- Monthly Shift Schedule: The monthly shift schedule must be assigned via the online system within 4 working days of the start of each month.
- Emergency Shift Changes: Up to three emergency shift changes per month may be approved, provided they are not related to routine personal activities. Prior approval from the Department Head is required through the online system.
## Weekly Off Change:
- Emergency Off Change: One off change per month is allowed in cases of emergency, subject to prior approval from the Department Head through the online system.
- Weekly Off Assignment: Weekly off days will be assigned through the online system within 4 working days of the start of each month. A maximum of 4-5 weekly offs can be taken per month, depending on the length of the month.
- Intervening Weekly Off & LWP: Any weekly off or paid holiday falling within a period of absenteeism or LWP will be treated as an absence.

chapters.title: Bonus:
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Employees who have worked a minimum of 30 working days during the year are eligible for a bonus. The bonus year is from 1st April to 31st March.
- Bonus Calculation: Employees with a basic salary of up to Rs. 10,000 are eligible for a minimum bonus of 8.33% of the higher of salary or basic wages earned during the accounting year.
- Payment of Bonus: Bonus will be paid within 8 months from the end of the accounting year. Employees who leave the organization during the year will receive their bonus as part of the full and final settlement.

## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy - Rakheja Enterprises LLP
- All employees at Rakheja Enterprises LLP must record their daily attendance to ensure precise payroll processing. Attendance is recorded using our Attendance Recording System (ARS), which includes Face Recognition or Touch Screen Machines at all company locations, fostering a culture of trust, integrity, and self-discipline.
- Employees are expected to clock in and out at scheduled times using the ARS. In cases of technical issues, manual sign-in is required, noting arrival and departure.
- To encourage punctuality, employees should arrive before shifts start. Heads of Department (HODs) must maintain a minimum presence of 8 hours daily.
- A 15-minute grace period is allowed up to 3 times per month for lateness (e.g., vehicle issues or personal matters). Beyond this, leave deduction applies, and if no leave balance is available, it will be marked as Leave Without Pay (LWP).
- Employees may arrive late or leave early (up to 2 hours) twice monthly for emergencies. Further occurrences lead to deductions or require a half-day leave.
- A minimum of 3.5 hours counts as a half-day; less will count as a full absence, based on grace period rules. Lateness exceeding 2 hours results in marking a half-day absence.
- Employees leaving for official or personal tasks during work hours must apply for a Gate Pass. Employees should swipe their attendance card on leaving and returning.
- If unable to return before office hours after official work, attendance can be regularized the next working day upon supervisor approval and Gate Pass submission.
- Travel-related Attendance: Attendance for domestic, international, or off-site work is regularized through HR based on Travel Indent Form and HOD approval.
- Employees are expected to plan and apply for leave beforehand for smoother attendance regularization.
- In emergencies where leave applications can’t be submitted in advance, the HR Department accepts applications within four working days post-return; after this, it will be marked as Absent Without Pay.
- For half-day leaves (second half of the shift), employees must obtain and submit an authorized Gate Pass to security at departure.
- Emergency departures during a shift require a Gate Pass and permission from the superior, submitted to security for premises exit.
Overtime
- Overtime is recorded in the ARS for accurate payroll tracking, compensated at 1.5 times the regular hourly wage.
- Employees should seek prior supervisor authorization for overtime. Unapproved overtime may not be compensated.
- Any overtime beyond standard hours requires justification and department head approval. Only necessary overtime aligned with operational needs is encouraged.
## Terms and Conditions:
- Overtime requires prior HOD approval in writing, with last-minute requests allowed only for exceptional cases (e.g., client meetings, urgent deadlines, audits).
- Efforts should be made to avoid compensatory time by adjusting hours within the same week.
- Shift changes for personal work are not considered overtime.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements - Rakheja Enterprises LLP
chapters.text:
Rakheja Enterprises LLP supports flexible working arrangements to promote work-life balance, provided operational needs are met. This policy applies to all employees impacted by company operations.
## Types of Flexible Arrangements
- Flexitime: Allows employees to adjust start and end times within set hours, accommodating personal needs.
- Remote Work: Employees may work from alternative locations, contingent on necessary equipment availability.
- Job Sharing: Two or more employees share a full-time role, each working part-time, allowing flexibility and growth opportunities.
## Eligibility
Employees must meet the following criteria to qualify for flexible working arrangements:
- Have completed at least six months of continuous service at Rakheja Enterprises LLP.
- Demonstrate the ability to meet performance expectations and maintain productivity.
- Have no ongoing disciplinary actions or performance improvement plans.
- Hold a role that is suitable for the requested flexible arrangement, as determined by the department head.
- Have access to the required resources and technology for the arrangement.
## Employee Responsibilities
## Employees
- Maintain productivity and time management.
- Communicate schedules and changes clearly with managers.
- Adhere to in-office days, mandatory meetings, and professional communication standards.
- Follow data security protocols and report any issues promptly.
## Department Heads
- Set clear expectations, including core hours and deliverables.
- Ensure remote employees have necessary tools, review performance, and monitor flexible arrangement effectiveness.
- Facilitate regular check-ins and encourage collaboration using communication tools.
## Application and Approval Process
- Request Submission: Employees submit requests through the designated form, outlining the arrangement type, schedule, justification, and productivity plan.
- Approval Process: Department heads review within two days, with HR making final decisions within an additional two days. Trial periods of 1-3 months evaluate arrangement effectiveness.
## Guidelines for Employees
- Remote employees should establish dedicated workspaces and maintain regular communication. Attend required meetings and ensure work quality.
## Non-Compliance
- Non-compliance includes delays in communication, absence from meetings, inadequate performance, or misuse of equipment.
- Consequences range from warnings to corrective action, and repeated non-compliance may result in flexible arrangement revocation or disciplinary action.
## Record Keeping and Review
- All applications and approvals are documented, with biennial HR reviews assessing the flexible work framework's impact on productivity and employee satisfaction.
## Transparent remuneration Process
At Rakheja Enterprises LLP, we are committed to ensuring transparency in our remuneration process, ensuring all employees are aware of their salary, benefits, and any additional compensation they may receive. The following outlines how remuneration is determined, communicated, and processed.

chapters.title: Salary Structure
chapters.text:
- Offer Letter Salary: The salary mentioned in your offer letter is the starting point for your compensation. This amount is clearly defined based on your position, qualifications, experience, and industry standards.
- Online Company Portal: Employees can view their current salary, benefits, and other compensation details through the company's secure online portal. This portal provides real-time access to your salary breakdown, including base pay, allowances, bonuses, and other compensations.
- Salary Bands: Salaries are organized into defined bands based on role and experience. These bands ensure that salaries are competitive and fair within the industry and are aligned with your job level. The band you fall within is outlined in your offer letter and can be referenced at any time via the online portal.
## Performance-Based Increments
- Annual Performance Reviews: Salary increments are linked to annual performance reviews, where your achievements, contributions, and growth are assessed. A percentage increase in salary is determined based on these evaluations.
- Review and Update Process: Performance reviews and salary adjustments are communicated transparently via the online portal and through one-on-one meetings with your manager. If you are eligible for a salary increase, it will be clearly stated in your review documents and updated on the portal.
## Bonuses and Incentives
- Annual Bonus: Employees may be eligible for an annual performance-based bonus, which is tied to company and individual performance metrics. Details of eligibility, criteria, and payout are outlined at the beginning of each fiscal year, and bonuses will be reflected on the employee’s payslip.
- Spot Awards and Special Incentives: Exceptional contributions may be rewarded through spot awards or other special incentives. Information about such incentives is communicated via internal announcements and can be accessed through the company portal.
- Overtime Compensation: Overtime hours worked will be compensated at the appropriate rate and reflected in the monthly payslip. The online portal will display overtime details for transparency.
## Leave and Time-Off
- Leave Balances: Your leave balance (annual leave, sick leave, etc.) is tracked and updated regularly in the online portal. You can view your leave status and apply for leave directly through the portal.
- Leave Approval: All leave requests must be submitted via the portal. Once approved by your supervisor, the leave will be reflected in your payroll calculations.
## Payroll Process
- Salary Payments: Salaries are processed monthly and are transferred directly to the bank account you’ve provided. Payment is typically made on the last working day of each month. Detailed payslips will be available through the online portal for your reference.
- Payslip Details: Your payslip includes your base salary, any bonuses, overtime, allowances, and deductions such as taxes, insurance premiums, and retirement contributions. It is updated monthly and available for download through the company portal.
- Transparent Deductions: Deductions for taxes and other statutory contributions will be clearly listed on your payslip. You can review these deductions and any changes to them at any time via the portal.
## Remuneration Review and Feedback
- Annual Salary Review: Rakheja Enterprises LLP conducts an annual review of all remuneration packages. Adjustments to salaries, bonuses, and benefits are communicated clearly through your performance evaluation and updated on the company portal.
- Employee Feedback: We encourage employees to provide feedback about the remuneration process through surveys and direct discussions with HR. Your feedback will help us ensure fairness and transparency in our compensation structure.
## Equal Pay for Equal Work
- Non-Discriminatory Pay: Rakheja Enterprises LLP is committed to providing equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or any other factors. Our salary structures are audited regularly to ensure compliance with this principle, and any discrepancies are addressed promptly.
- Career Advancement and Promotions: Clear guidelines regarding salary advancement, role promotion, and compensation for career progression are available in the portal. Employees can review these guidelines to understand how their remuneration evolves with their career growth.
## Clear and Open Communication
- Access to Remuneration Details: Employees have full access to their salary and remuneration details, including salary bands, bonuses, and performance incentives, through the secure online portal.
- Questions and Queries: If you have any questions about your salary, benefits, or remuneration process, you can contact HR directly or review your salary breakdown in the portal for clarity. HR is always available to provide assistance and ensure transparency.

chapters.title: Health and Wellness Benefits & Insurance Policy
chapters.text:
Rakheja Enterprises LLP offers a comprehensive health and wellness program designed to support the physical and mental well-being of its employees, with a strong emphasis on preventive care, emergency support, and overall work-life balance. The following outlines the key benefits provided and the associated insurance coverage details:
Health and Wellness Benefits:
- Comprehensive Medical Insurance: Rakheja Enterprises provides medical insurance with coverage up to ₹5,00,000 annually for each employee, covering hospitalization, surgeries, and treatment for both employees and their dependents (spouse, children, and parents). Employees can enhance their coverage at discounted premiums through the company’s health coverage partner.
- Cashless Treatment Network: Employees can access cashless treatment at over 5,000 hospitals across the country, ensuring smooth and efficient access to care during emergencies.
- Mental Health Support: Rakheja Enterprises values mental well-being and offers confidential counseling services through certified professionals. Employees are eligible for free therapy sessions and access stress management workshops.
- Fitness and Wellness Programs: The company encourages physical fitness by offering free gym memberships or fitness app subscriptions, on-site or virtual yoga and meditation sessions, and wellness challenges with fitness rewards.
- Annual Health Check-Ups: Employees and their dependents are entitled to free annual health screenings, including blood tests, vision checks, cholesterol monitoring, and other preventive diagnostics.
- Dental and Vision Coverage: In addition to medical coverage, optional dental and vision plans are available, covering routine dental work, eye exams, and prescription lenses.
- Wellness Resources and Seminars: Employees have access to a wellness platform with curated articles, videos, and self-help tools on fitness, nutrition, and mental health. Monthly wellness seminars with healthcare experts are also hosted.
- Critical Illness and Accident Insurance: Employees are automatically enrolled in critical illness insurance, which provides lump-sum payouts for conditions such as cancer, heart disease, or stroke. Accidental insurance covers medical expenses and loss of income, offering up to ₹10,00,000 in the case of permanent disability or death.
- Work-Life Balance Initiatives: Rakheja Enterprises promotes work-life balance with flexible work schedules, remote working options, and employee assistance programs (EAP) to support both personal and professional well-being.
Health and Accident Insurance Coverage:
Objective: To provide comprehensive health and accident insurance coverage for eligible employees, addressing medical expenses, hospitalization, and accidents occurring during work or while commuting.
Scope: This policy applies to all full-time employees working in the office premises of Rakheja Enterprises LLP, who are not covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.
Responsibility: The Head of HR & Administration is responsible for implementing this policy in collaboration with the Finance department and CEO.
Eligibility:
- Employees, their spouses, and up to two dependent children under 25 years.
- Employees may cover either both parents or both in-laws (up to 90 years), but not a combination of both.
- Employees must have completed a minimum of 90 days of continuous service with the company to be eligible for coverage.
Coverage Details:
- ₹5 Lakhs total medical insurance.
- ₹10 Lakhs total accidental insurance.
Coverage Inclusions:
- Medical expenses for daycare treatments, hospitalization, and domiciliary care.
- Optional Add-On Covers:
- Pre-existing conditions.
- Maternity expenses.
- Critical illness.
- Outpatient treatments.
- Dental treatments.
- Organ transplant expenses.
- Ambulance and air ambulance services.
- Health check-ups.
- Modern treatments.
- Wage loss compensation during hospitalization.
Accident Insurance Coverage:
- Coverage includes accidental death, permanent or partial disability resulting from workplace accidents or commuting, and related medical expenses.
Waiting Period:
- Pre-existing conditions are covered after 1 year.
- Maternity benefits are subject to a 9-month waiting period.
Exclusions:
- Cosmetic treatments and dental care (unless linked to hospitalization).
- Self-inflicted injuries and voluntary pregnancy termination under 12 weeks.
- Full policy details for further exclusions.
Payment Basis:
- Claims can be processed via cashless or reimbursement methods, depending on the sum insured.
Cost Sharing:
- Employees may share costs for expenses exceeding sub-limits or room rent limits.
Renewal & Cancellation:
- The policy can be renewed annually or canceled by either party with prior notice. Fraud or non-disclosure of key facts can lead to termination.
Claims Procedure:
- Cashless claims are available at designated hospitals.
- Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 30 days of treatment.

chapters.title: Anti-Discrimination Policy
chapters.text:
- Equal Opportunity Employment: Rakheja Enterprises LLP values equal opportunity, making employment decisions based on merit and performance. Our hiring, promotions, compensation, and training practices are free from biases related to race, gender, age, disability, religion, or any other protected characteristic.
- Prohibited Conduct: We prohibit any form of discrimination, including biased hiring practices, pay disparities, or restricted access to career growth.
- Reasonable Accommodation: We offer accommodations to employees with disabilities or those needing religious accommodations. The HR Department will work with employees to ensure these accommodations meet both their needs and company capabilities.
- Policy Enforcement: We take all complaints seriously, thoroughly investigating each and implementing disciplinary measures, from counselling to termination, as needed.
## Examples of Discrimination:
- Unequal Pay: A qualified employee receiving less pay than their colleagues performing the same job based on gender or ethnicity.
- Unequal Opportunities: A qualified employee being overlooked for a promotion based on their age or disability, despite their strong qualifications and performance.

chapters.title: Anti-Harassment Policy
chapters.text:
- Definition of Harassment: Harassment includes any unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct creating a hostile or uncomfortable work environment.
## Types of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Unwelcome sexual advances, inappropriate comments, physical gestures, or requests for sexual favors. This type of harassment creates an uncomfortable and unsafe environment for the individual being targeted.
- Bullying: Repeated, unreasonable actions intended to undermine or intimidate an individual. This can include verbal abuse, spreading false rumors, or deliberately sabotaging someone's work or reputation.
- Retaliation: Any adverse action taken against an employee who has reported harassment or participated in an investigation. Retaliation may include unjustified disciplinary actions, exclusion from team activities, or denial of career advancement opportunities.
## Examples of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Sending inappropriate or unsolicited messages to a colleague, creating a hostile work environment.
- Bullying: Making derogatory comments about a colleague’s race or gender, undermining their performance and confidence.
- Retaliation: Taking disciplinary actions or sidelining an employee who reported harassment, deterring others from coming forward.
- Support for Victims: We offer support to employees who have experienced harassment, including counselling services and the option to adjust work arrangements if necessary. Ensuring that victims feel protected and supported is a key part of our commitment to maintaining a respectful work environment.
- Training and Education: Regular training sessions are conducted for all employees, focusing on our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies. The training educates employees on how to recognize harassment, the importance of reporting concerns, and how to foster a positive and inclusive workplace.
## Responsibilities and Compliance
- Employee Responsibilities: Employees are expected to report discrimination or harassment promptly.
- Manager Responsibilities: Managers must uphold and enforce this policy, create a safe environment, and address complaints swiftly.
- Monitoring and Review: Regular reviews and updates to the policy ensure it reflects legal requirements and employee feedback.
- Consequences: Violations may lead to disciplinary actions, up to termination.
## Preventive Measures
- Clear Communication of Policy: At Rakheja Enterprises LLP, all employees are provided with a copy of the Harassment Prevention Policy during onboarding and through regular training sessions. This ensures that everyone is well-informed about unacceptable behaviors and understands the potential consequences of such actions.
- Regular Risk Assessments: We conduct regular assessments to identify and evaluate any potential harassment risks within the workplace. This proactive approach helps us address vulnerabilities before they become significant issues.
- Anonymous Reporting Channels: To promote a safe reporting environment, we offer confidential and anonymous reporting options. This encourages employees to report any incidents of harassment without fear of retaliation.
- Active Monitoring: Rakheja Enterprises LLP implements monitoring systems to observe workplace interactions and detect behaviors that may indicate harassment. We hold regular feedback sessions to evaluate our workplace culture and address any emerging concerns promptly.
- Support Systems: We have established various support resources, such as peer support groups and counselling services, to assist employees who may need help in dealing with harassment or other workplace issues.
## Reporting Procedure
Rakheja Enterprises LLP takes all allegations of discrimination and harassment seriously. To ensure the reporting process is accessible and straightforward, we provide multiple channels for employees to raise concerns:
- Direct Reporting: Report incidents to immediate supervisors or the Head of Human Resources.
- Anonymous Reporting: Use the confidential reporting system if preferred.
- Handbook Reference: The Employee Handbook provides step-by-step guidance on reporting and resources.
## Two-Way Communication Sessions Policy
## Objective
This policy establishes clear communication channels between employees and management, promoting transparency and giving employees a voice regarding working conditions and benefits.
## Scope
Applicable to all employees, the policy aims to encourage engagement and transparency across the company.
## Responsibilities
The HR Department organizes sessions, encouraging managers and executives, including senior leadership, to participate actively.
## Types of Two-Way Communication Sessions
- Company-Wide Forums (Town Halls): Quarterly meetings with senior management and employees, allowing open dialogue.
- Departmental Feedback Sessions: Monthly discussions within departments for specific issues.

chapters.title: Training & Development at Rakheja Enterprises LLP
chapters.text:
## Objective:
The aim of this training program is to ensure that employees at Rakheja Enterprises receive appropriate training to enhance their performance, specifically in Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and their respective roles. The program ensures proper documentation of all training sessions and provides a structured procedure for identifying, planning, executing, and tracking employee training in the manufacturing and support functions.
## Scope:
This training approach applies to both new and existing employees, including permanent and contract staff working in various functions such as manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering, and quality assurance at Rakheja Enterprises LLP facilities.
## Roles and Responsibilities:
## Training Coordinator:
- Oversees the training process for new hires and ensures that on-the-job training is completed before employees start their routine tasks.
- Manages and schedules periodic cGMP training for all employees.
- Develops training plans for cGMP and functional training across various departments.
- Identifies and qualifies trainers within the company, ensuring that the training pool is adequately staffed.
- Coordinates the creation of training materials and facilitates training sessions.
- Tracks employee training progress and escalates issues when necessary.
## Department Training Coordinators:
- Responsible for identifying specific training needs related to departmental Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Monitors the progress of employees' training, ensuring timely completion, and reports any delays to the Training Coordinator.
## nstructors/Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
- Conduct training sessions and share their expertise on relevant topics.
- Serve as primary trainers and facilitate knowledge transfer.
## Human Resources:
- Coordinates the induction training programs for new employees, both onsite and offsite.
- Ensures that all new hires complete the necessary induction and onboarding processes.
## Employees:
- Are responsible for completing all assigned training within the specified timelines.
- Participate actively in training sessions and engage with learning materials.
## Training Procedures:
- Training: This process involves the acquisition of knowledge, skills, and competencies required to improve performance in specific job functions. It includes theoretical and practical learning aimed at enhancing employee capabilities.
- Training Needs Identification (TNI): This process helps to identify the training requirements for each role. Training needs are documented and assigned to employees based on their job functions and personal development goals, ensuring that they are equipped to perform their tasks efficiently.
- Training Management System: The system is designed to manage the administration, delivery, documentation, tracking, and reporting of training programs. This includes classroom training, online sessions, e-learning, and other training resources.
## Training for New Permanent Employees:
- Induction Training: All new employees will undergo an initial induction program when joining Rakheja Enterprises LLP. This training introduces employees to the organization, its policies, and its core functions, as well as health, safety, and environmental protocols. A site-specific induction manual may be prepared for each department to tailor the training content.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution Procedure for Rakheja Enterprises LLP
chapters.text:
Purpose The purpose of establishing this grievance resolution procedure is to provide employees with a formal and structured process to raise concerns related to their job, manager, or the work environment. These concerns can range from perceived unfair treatment to issues related to safety or discrimination. By offering a clear and transparent grievance process, Rakheja Enterprises LLP ensures that employees have a safe space to voice their issues, and these concerns are properly addressed. This procedure aims to identify and resolve workplace issues, thereby fostering a positive and productive work environment.
## Key Benefits
- Fairness and Accessibility: Ensures all employees have equal access to report concerns.
- Transparency: Promotes openness in addressing and resolving grievances.
- Problem Identification: Helps uncover underlying issues that may not be immediately visible.
- Risk Mitigation & Compliance: Reduces potential legal or financial risks associated with unresolved grievances.
- Better Decision-Making: Informed decisions based on facts, improving company policies and practices.
- Improved Workplace: Contributes to a more harmonious and productive environment.
- Enhanced Employee Engagement: Promotes a culture of trust and respect, increasing employee satisfaction.
- Strengthened Organizational Culture: Reinforces company values of fairness, inclusivity, and respect.
- Legal Protection and Reduced Liability: Provides legal safeguards by addressing concerns systematically and reducing the risk of legal disputes.
This includes all employees, regardless of their position, as well as contractors, suppliers, and community members impacted by the company’s operations.
## Definitions
- Grievance: A grievance refers to any work-related issue raised by an employee, perceived as unfair treatment, violation of rights, or any other workplace concern that is detrimental to their well-being, such as unsafe working conditions, unequal pay, harassment, or discrimination.
- Grievance Mechanism: This is the formal, structured process that Rakheja Enterprises LLP has put in place to ensure that grievances are addressed in a timely, fair, and confidential manner. The grievance mechanism ensures that employees’ concerns are heard and acted upon appropriately.
## Types of Grievances:
Employee grievances may vary but generally fall into the following categories:
- Pay and Benefits: Issues related to salary discrepancies, bonuses, benefits, or payroll errors.
- Working Conditions: Concerns about unsafe, unhealthy, or unpleasant work environments, or unfair scheduling practices.
- Treatment: Issues such as harassment, discrimination, bullying, or lack of recognition from management.
- Workload: Feelings of being overwhelmed with work, insufficient resources, or inadequate support to meet job expectations.
- Communication: Concerns about unclear communication, lack of feedback, or the perception that management is not listening to employees.
Other specific grievances that may arise include:

Reporting Methods Employees can report grievances through various methods:
- Human Resources Department: The HR team is responsible for managing grievances. Employees are encouraged to report their issues using one of the following methods:
- Direct Reporting to HR Manager: Employees can directly approach HR or contact the HR Manager by email at hr@Rakheja Enterprises.com.
- Department Head: In cases where it is deemed appropriate, employees can report grievances to their immediate department head.
- Grievance Reporting Boxes: To provide anonymity, employees can submit written grievances using designated reporting boxes placed throughout the company premises.
Record Keeping For transparency and to ensure a fair resolution process, all grievances and their resolutions will be documented systematically. This includes:
- Filing System: Each grievance will have a separate folder that includes details like the employee’s name (unless reported anonymously), a brief description of the issue, and a chronological history of the grievance.
- Electronic Storage: All electronic records related to grievances will be stored securely, using encryption to ensure that only authorized personnel have access to the data.
- Backup: Regular backups of grievance records will be performed quarterly to ensure data security.
## Key Documents to Retain:
- The initial grievance form or complaint.
- Correspondence, meeting notes, and emails.
- Investigation materials such as witness statements and evidence.
- Records of any actions or decisions taken during the grievance process.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
Purpose The purpose of this Whistleblower Procedure is to provide a secure and confidential way for employees and external parties to report ethical concerns, promoting transparency, integrity, and accountability. Rakheja Enterprises LLP is committed to safeguarding its reputation, assets, and stakeholders by upholding the highest ethical standards across all operations.
## Scope
This procedure applies to all individuals associated with Rakheja Enterprises LLP, including employees, contractors, consultants, vendors, suppliers, and third parties. It ensures uniform handling of ethical issues across all company locations.
## Reporting Criteria
Concerns to report include, but are not limited to:
- Corruption: Activities such as bribery, fraud, or embezzlement that may compromise the company’s integrity.
- Bribery: Any improper exchange of value to influence decisions.
- Information Security: Unauthorized data access, breaches, or IT security violations.
- Discrimination and Harassment: Violations of equal opportunity laws, harassment policies, or discriminatory practices.
- Policy Violations: Breaches that may impact Rakheja Enterprises LLP's reputation, create legal risks, or affect operational efficiency.
## Reporting Channels
Rakheja Enterprises LLP provides several reporting options:
- Direct Reporting: Concerns can be reported directly to senior management or HR.
- Contact Number: +91-124-4341700
- Anonymous Reporting: Anonymous submissions are accepted via email.
## Email: concerns@rakhejaenterprises.com
## Procedure
- Initial Assessment: HR reviews the report within two business days.
- Evidence Gathering: Relevant evidence is collected within five business days.
- Interviews: Witnesses or involved parties are interviewed within ten business days.
- Analysis and Review: Findings are analyzed within seven business days.
- Actions and Resolution: HR determines and implements actions within 15 business days.
- Outcome Communication: Findings are communicated to the reporter within three business days after a decision.
## Responsibilities
- Employees: Report concerns in good faith, cooperate in investigations, and avoid false accusations.
- Management: Ensure awareness of the policy, respond to reports seriously, and ensure appropriate action based on findings.
## Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation
- Confidentiality: All reports are treated with strict confidentiality.
- Non-Retaliation: Retaliation against whistleblowers is strictly prohibited and will lead to disciplinary action.
